q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM (SELECT DISTINCT STUDENT , CLASS FROM COURSES)T1 GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(CLASS)>= 5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM (SELECT DISTINCT STUDENT , CLASS FROM COURSES)T1 GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(CLASS)>= 5
explanation: Q1 groups by CLASS and counts all rows where COUNT(*) >= 5. Q2 groups by CLASS after removing duplicate (STUDENT, CLASS) pairs, so it counts distinct students per class. Thus, Q2 counts distinct students per class while Q1 counts all enrollments per class. These can yield different results.
counterexample_dsp: A class with 5 enrollments from 3 distinct students would be excluded by Q2 but included by Q1.
